implementation.installedSpec: The terminal plugin bundled completionSpecs/go.json is loaded by the installed ShellCommandSpecsManagerImpl.
implementation.inputSource: The active TerminalOutputModel line at the terminal cursor. The reworked input text is not present in Editor.document while it is being typed.
implementation.replacement: TerminalInput.sendBytes(0x15) clears the shell edit line, then TerminalInput.sendString writes the completed command. This is a real PTY edit, not a visual-only action.
implementation.ranking: Go subcommands: test, telemetry, tool, build and the remaining standard commands. The first prefix match wins; go te therefore becomes go test.
implementation.testOptions: -run, -bench, -count, -race, -cover, coverage controls, JSON/verbose/status controls, build flags and execution flags.
implementation.startupDefaults: A one-time migration enables the completion popup, ALWAYS showing mode and IDE shortcut override without rewriting later user choices.
implementation.removedWorkaround: The redundant custom commandSpecsProvider and temporary shell-environment mutation were removed after the fallback was verified in both zsh and bash.

automatedVerification.fullGate: test, buildPlugin, prepareSandbox and verifyPluginStructure passed.

platformInspection.observedPlatformContract: ShellCommandSpecsManagerImpl reads commandSpecsProvider extensions and the bundled completion database. TerminalCommandCompletion.isEnabled requires local monolith mode, local EEL and the terminal completion registry.
platformInspection.rootCause: For the user Powerlevel10k zsh session, TerminalView.shellIntegrationDeferred never completed. TerminalCommandCompletionTypingListener therefore did not invoke the platform service even though the terminal itself was usable.
platformInspection.rejectedFix: Setting POWERLEVEL9K_INSTANT_PROMPT=off in a test process did not complete shell integration. The product therefore does not mutate the user shell environment.
platformInspection.fallbackDesign: Read the active output model, resolve a Go command line independently of shell-integration markers, and send the replacement through the terminal input channel.

evidenceBoundary: This verifies deterministic Go command/option insertion on macOS with the user zsh profile and the built-in Bash profile. It does not claim a visible multi-candidate lookup, Windows terminal parity, remote/WSL shells, every custom prompt, or complete GoLand terminal parity.
nextProbe: Add an explicit candidate chooser for ambiguous prefixes, then verify the same behavior in Windows Terminal/ConPTY and at least one remote or WSL terminal.

runs.shell: zsh with the user Powerlevel10k profile
zsh with the user Powerlevel10k profile

nativeVerification.visibleLookup: No multi-candidate popup was observed. The fallback deterministically inserts the first ranked candidate so completion remains usable when the platform lookup cannot open.
nativeVerification.classification: Native Go command and test-option auto-completion is accepted for the verified macOS shells.

previousFailedAttempts.summary: Platform-only popup attempts were superseded after shell integration was identified as the failed prerequisite.
observed: No Go subcommand popup appeared after opening new terminals with automatic completion enabled.
Tab fell back to zsh path completion and produced go _test.go.
Control+Space is intercepted by macOS input-source handling. Temporary test-only mappings for Terminal.CommandCompletion.Invoke on Control+Option+K and F2 did not visibly open the popup.
A temporary Go Terminal Completion menu action invoked Terminal.CommandCompletion.Invoke in terminal context but still produced no popup. The temporary action was removed before the final full gate.
A packaged candidate switched to the classic terminal engine still fell back to shell path completion for go te, so changing the engine alone does not close the native action-state gap.
